<!--
  The <head> tags every Argus front end needs for an iPhone (design-system#137).
  Copy the tags below into your index.html <head>. Apps that hand-copy these drift.

  viewport-fit=cover   Lets the page draw to the display edge, and is what makes
                       env(safe-area-inset-*) non-zero at all. Without it the
                       --safe-* tokens are always 0. Pair it with px-edge, pb-edge
                       and pt-safe so content stays out of the curves and notch.
                       The tag sets no zoom limit, so pinch zoom stays on (WCAG 1.4.4).
                       Do not add one.
  apple-mobile-web-app-* The Home Screen web app set. "default" status bar keeps the
                       bar opaque, so the top inset is the system's to manage;
                       the translucent style would make every app clear it itself. iOS 26 opens
                       every Home Screen site as a web app, so -capable matters only
                       on older iOS; the status-bar style decides the top inset
                       either way.
  theme-color          One per colour scheme; they match the default (Ocean) theme's
                       --background. Change them if the app sets another theme.
  the script tag      Dynamic Type (design-system#163). On iOS it measures the system
                       body font and sets --dt-scale on <html> (1 at the default Larger
                       Text size); the theme's guarded `html` rule multiplies the root
                       font by it, so rem text and spacing follow Larger Text, installed
                       PWAs included. Elsewhere it does nothing. Without it the root font
                       stays at the browser default. Keep it in <head>, so the first
                       paint is already at the right size.
  the second script   The status-bar band (design-system#167). The two theme-color tags above
                       give the right first paint, but an installed iOS web app may not
                       re-read them when it resumes after the system switches between
                       light and dark, and the band stays the old colour until a relaunch.
                       This script replaces them with one unscoped theme-color, and sets
                       color-scheme on <html>, from the resolved mode: the app's own dark
                       class once the theme init has set data-theme, else the system. It
                       re-applies on pageshow, visibilitychange, a system mode change and a
                       change of the dark class, inserting a fresh tag each time because
                       WebKit is known to notice an inserted meta before an edited one. It
                       reads the colours from the two tags, so changing them is enough.
                       Whether iOS re-reads the band on resume is a device check
                       (design-system#168); a page cannot confirm it. Keep it in <head>.
-->
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover" />
<meta name="mobile-web-app-capable" content="yes" />
<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-capable" content="yes" />
<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style" content="default" />
<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-title" content="App name" />
<meta name="theme-color" media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" content="#f5f7f8" />
<meta name="theme-color" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" content="#17212b" />
<script>
  (function () {
    var IOS_DEFAULT_BODY = 17
    if (!CSS.supports("font", "-apple-system-body") || !CSS.supports("-webkit-touch-callout", "none")) return
    var root = document.documentElement
    var measure = function () {
      var probe = document.createElement("span")
      probe.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true")
      probe.style.cssText = "position:absolute;visibility:hidden;font:-apple-system-body"
      root.appendChild(probe)
      var size = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(probe).fontSize)
      root.removeChild(probe)
      if (size > 0) root.style.setProperty("--dt-scale", String(Math.round((size / IOS_DEFAULT_BODY) * 1000) / 1000))
    }
    measure()
    addEventListener("pageshow", measure)
    addEventListener("resize", measure)
    document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", measure)
  })()
</script>
<script>
  (function () {
    if (typeof matchMedia !== "function") return
    var root = document.documentElement
    var system = matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")
    var declared = document.querySelectorAll('meta[name="theme-color"]')
    var colors = {}
    for (var index = 0; index < declared.length; index++) {
      var media = declared[index].getAttribute("media") || ""
      var content = declared[index].getAttribute("content")
      if (media.indexOf("dark") > -1) colors.dark = content
      else if (media.indexOf("light") > -1) colors.light = content
    }
    if (!colors.light || !colors.dark) return
    var apply = function () {
      var mode = (root.hasAttribute("data-theme") ? root.classList.contains("dark") : system.matches) ? "dark" : "light"
      var stale = document.querySelectorAll('meta[name="theme-color"]')
      for (var position = 0; position < stale.length; position++) stale[position].parentNode.removeChild(stale[position])
      var tag = document.createElement("meta")
      tag.setAttribute("name", "theme-color")
      tag.setAttribute("content", colors[mode])
      document.head.appendChild(tag)
      root.style.colorScheme = mode
    }
    apply()
    addEventListener("pageshow", apply)
    document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", apply)
    system.addEventListener("change", apply)
    if (typeof MutationObserver === "function") new MutationObserver(apply).observe(root, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ["class", "data-theme"] })
  })()
</script>
